analysis:
All changed files in this batch are test-only under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. No production source, keys, attestation, WebSocket protocol, prefix-cache crypto, or authorization code is modified here. The tests cover: benchmark report schema v5 (prefillChunkTokens/maxBatchedTokensPerStep) with schema-4 legacy decode; the benchmark checkpoint environment pinning prefill chunk 512 and step budget 2048 when a stripe is pinned; the live-runner engine environment pinning simulated geometry with an inherited 4096 chunk overridden; and Gemma/paged-KV gate tests asserting the wide plain chunk replaces the default solo-prefill stripe while the paged pool's maxPrefillChunk stays at max(chunk, stripe) (the default stripe size).

Security relevance: the production change implied by these tests (default stripe replaced by a wide plain chunk for Gemma 4, with the paged pool sized to the old stripe) concerns the engine scheduler and paged KV geometry (TB-007). The tests pin the lockstep invariant against pool-size aborts (an availability concern, T-010/T-029 class). I cannot see the production edits, so the correctness of that invariant for opt-in chunk/budget overrides, such as an environment-set chunk larger than the pool's maxPrefillChunk, is unverified. The test at the widePrefillChunkKeepsPagedPoolGeometry hunk shows a 2048 chunk with a pool chunk equal to the default stripe, but only for the tested values.

The T-041 prefix-cache surface (SSD tier, HMAC names, TTL, scope) is not touched by these tests. DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_TEST_ROOT appear only in benchmark fixture env assertions. No new attack surface, no regression, and no threat-model update is needed from the visible evidence. Remaining question for integration: whether the production EngineV2Factory change clamps or validates user-supplied prefillChunkKey/stepTokenBudgetKey against paged pool ring sizing.
